recipes.name: Sweet and Silky Strawberry Sorbet
ingredients_raw: 1 pound ripe strawberries, hulled and chopped

steps.text: Place berries in the bowl of a food processor and puree until smooth.
Transfer pureed strawberry mixture into a large saucepan over medium heat. Add sugar and salt; stir until dissolved and bring to a simmer.

Whisk cornstarch and cold water together in a small bowl until smooth; stir into simmering strawberry mixture. Remove the saucepan from heat, stir in lemon juice, and allow to cool slightly. Refrigerate strawberry mixture until cold, about 2 hours.
Freeze in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer's instructions, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Silky Strawberry Sorbet
raw_recipe.description: This easy sorbet recipe makes a sweet, soft, homemade strawberry sorbet to rival any brand you can buy in the grocery store!

review.reviewBody: Wonderful! I can't have strawberries, so I substituted other fruit. Also, I'm not very patient, so I cooled it off first in the fridge, then in the freezer (just until cool, not frozen) so I wouldn't have to wait 2 hours. It turned out great! I've been using All Recipes for years now, but this is the first recipe I felt strongly enough about to actually rate and review. This really does turn out just like store bought sorbet - which is getting harder to find in my area. Just what I was looking for!

Excellent!
I would just like to state that if you are using a standard sized home ice cream maker, you probably want to double this.
Also, the recipe works for any mixture of other fruits, my personal favorite being half strawberry, half pineapple. I also add about twice as much lemon juice.
I tend to use one freezer bowl for twenty minutes, then the other for twenty minutes to churn it effectively, but when using only the single recipe, the twenty minutes in one freezer bowl was fine.
Altogether a delicious sorbet, and it freezes more easily than most other recipes I've tried.

Great base recipie as is! I usually add some flavored vodka to prevent the sorbet to be frozen completely, helps when making it without an ice cream machine and flavors can be intermixed.. Watermelon Vodka (about 3 tbs) example. I used 1/2 fresh lemon and 3 tbsp orange juice in lieu of the cold water cornstarch mix.. Great flavor for a great recipie!

Delish and so easy. Thank you for sharing! I halved the sugar as my berries were very sweet already. I reduced the lemon as well - I think I used about 2 tablespoons - I added a tablespoon at a time until it tasted to my liking. I also used another reviewer's suggestion for making without an ice cream machine. I froze it in a parchment lined square metal baking pan and then let it thaw a little and ran it through the blender one more time and froze again. Let it thaw a few minutes before serving and it is smooth and tasty! Thanks again!

This is very good. We made it with white stevia powder instead of sugar. The Stevia in the Raw packet says that you can use it 1:1 with sugar but don't do it! I've been using stevia for 12 years, and so I used less than 1/2 cup, and it was still a little too sweet. Still, I would do this recipe again. Also, I used the recommendation someone else said and blended the frozen puree once. It turned out really well.

This was LOVELY. I doubled this recipe, used Splenda instead of sugar and I used a mixture of strawberries and blueberries. I don't have an ice cream maker so I froze it in a freezer container until solid, then scooped it back into my blender and re-blended it and then re-froze it. REALLY good, though I think the sweet could be cut back by at least a quarter next time. That's not a deal breaker, though.

This was fabulous in taste and consistency. You must vary the amount of lemon juice to the sweetness of your berries or fruit. Less sweet berries will require less lemon juice, and I would only use 1.5 Tbsp max, but that is my preference. It does need some, no matter what. Also, you will find that substituting 2 Tbsp of the sugar with 2 Tbsp corn syrup will produce an even silkier texture. And dressing each serving with a small amount of chiffonaded fresh basil not only adds color, but a nice flavor complement as well. Thank you, Dana, for a terrific recipe I will use again and again!

I made this great sorbet in the summer, Its soft, silky, and sweet. But I did use powdered sugar, which made it taste less gridy. Then instead of cornstarch I used arrow-root starch, And just by using those two things its texture and flavor was ten times better! Thanks for the great recipe:)

Loved this,great basis for other fruit sorbets,I have tried it with ripe peaches,and subbed orange for lemon juice,was also excellent.and used cornfour instead of cornstarch,could be same thing,but here in NZ we have different names for a few things!

I have never been satisfied with a strawberry sorbet recipe until this one. I did sub powdered sugar for the granulated so I didn't have to cook it so long, but the only other changes were adjustments in the amounts of sugar and lemon juice because of the sweetness of the berries. I made it for a church ice cream social, and got a lot of compliments on it.

I served this to a dinner party, and was told by people that this was the best sorbet they had ever had! excellent, & easy to boot! note: I didnt use the food processor- I used frozen strawberrys, heated them up, added sugar, & used a pastry blender to mash them up before adding other stuff. awesome!

It truly is hard to find a good sorbet recipe but this one nailed it. The sorbet came out delicious and not like an icy slushie at all. It already tastes so good with just out-of-season strawberries, I can only imagine how good it’ll be once we go out to pick them in summertime. I plan to serve it with some crepes next time, because why not.

Pretty tasty! Mine was tart though so I may have to downplay the lemon and up the sugar ... ? I used the full amount of lemon, fresh, but used maple sugar instead of white sugar. I also put flour in instead of cornstarch (can't have corn). It turned out really yummy from just my freezer but a bit jam tasting. Consistency was great a couple hours in the freezer; I hope it keeps well in there so it can be my new non-dairy ice cream treat! Want to try with peaches and raspberries next!
served it to guests for a light dessert.. everyone loved it.
OMG!!! The best sorbet recipe ever. I reused the recipe for other fruits, it works!
Very easy to make and flavor was great.
Awesome!
No changes needed. Absolutely delicious! Just the right tang with lemon juice. Friends ate up in one fell swoop. Will make over and over again, for sure.....Thanks for sharing...
this was a great recipe, but the only thing that I didn't like was that the recipe made a very little amount of sorbet, and we were all wishing there was more

Recpie works as provided, but allows for ajustment for personal taste. Will regularly make this summer with different fruits and fruit combination. Today made Strawberry and Pineapple, fantastic results.
